description:
FILED AND FIXED s473t5a (#1501 CHECK 1 round 2, 2026-09-13), found while
attributing t/op/sub_lval.t's 116-row shortfall.

    $ cat d.pl
    no strict 'vars';
    sub g2 { @119797 }
    print "d=[@119797]\n";

    perl: d=[]
    pcl : The variable @119797 is unbound.   (and the whole top-level form dies)

perl names a package ARRAY or HASH with digits perfectly happily -- only the
`$` spelling is magic there (`$119797` is capture group 119797, read-only;
probed: `$119798 = "s"` is "Modification of a read-only value attempted" in
perl AND in PCL, which already gets that right).  `@1`, `%2` and `@119797` are
ordinary containers, and `$main::{'1'}` exists after `@1 = (7,8)`.

WHY IT CRASHED.  `Pl/Parser2.pm`'s free-global scan -- the pass that emits
";; Forward declarations for undeclared package globals" -- matched
`[\$\@\%][A-Za-z_]\w*+`, a LETTER-or-underscore head.  So a digit-headed name
was never declared, and the emitted `@119797` was a bare, unbound CL symbol.
It only showed up when the name is never ASSIGNED at segment top level (an
assignment declares it on the ordinary path), which is why t/op/sub_lval.t's
[perl #119797] fixture -- `sub else119797 : lvalue { … @119797 … }` plus reads
-- hit it and `@119797 = (1,2,3)` at top level did not.

THE FIX.  ONE new reading, `$Pl::Parser2::VAR_TOKEN_RX`, consumed by BOTH
scans in that pass -- the unqualified one and the cross-package one, which had
each spelled the name class for themselves and were therefore blind in the same
way one `::` apart (`@Bar::424242` crashed too, measured on the base).  The
class is "any sigil + letter/underscore head, OR `@`/`%` + digit head"; the
possessive `\w*+` (#415) is preserved.  The `$` sigil deliberately keeps the
letter head so the capture family stays runtime-owned.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3, all identical after the fix and the last two CRASHING
on a `git archive 8c8fa4c0` extraction:
  - `@119797` read in a sub and at file level, never assigned      (crash -> [])
  - `@Bar::424242` read, never assigned                            (crash -> [])
  - `@1 = (7,8)` / `@119797 = (1,2,3)` assigned then read          (already OK)
  - `$1` after a match, and `$119798 = "s"` (read-only error)      (unchanged)

Guard: `Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t` (the row names it).  Emission over the four
populations is unchanged except where such a name occurs, so no generation
consequence beyond the batch's.

RESIDUE, NOT THIS TASK: `%119799 = (k => 'v')` is still a loud DROP ("Handle
single node of unknown type") -- the term walker declines a digit-headed HASH
in an assignment target.  It is a PExpr gap, not a declaration gap, and it was
a drop before and after this change.  t/op/sub_lval.t's remaining 112 rows are
not-supported.md section "Lvalue subroutines" (nine of its eleven aborted
top-level forms) plus one "Bug. Fell through. Missing case" on
`sub x : lvalue {…} continue {…}`.
subject: An ALL-DIGIT container name (`@119797`, `%42`) was never forward-declared, so reading it died "The variable @119797 is unbound" and took its whole top-level form -- FIXED s473t5a
